positions.catalyst: Tier 2 GOLD REVERSED HIGHER THIS MORNING AND THIS IS THE LARGEST PRODUCER - THE ONLY LEG IN THE BOOK THAT PAYS OFF ON A DE-ESCALATION FAILURE *AND* ON AN INFLATION SURPRISE: gold futures opened 9/9 at $4,399 an ounce, down 0.9% from Tuesday's close after US strikes on Iranian oil tankers, then reversed to $4,435.60 by 6:16am ET - a $36 intraday recovery that says the safe-haven bid is being defended rather than sold. Newmont is quoted with a 128.16 bid against a 127.09 close, and on 9/8 it traded 9.02M shares against an 8.18M 30-day average (1.10x) while running to a 130.035 high. The specific reason to own gold in THIS book is structural: eleven of my positions are levered to Middle East energy in one direction, and gold is the one asset that also rises if the conflict escalates - so it partially hedges the correlated de-escalation risk rather than adding to it. The catalyst-defined exit is the 9/11 CPI print at 8:30am ET, with consensus at 3.4% headline and 2.4% core.
positions.risks: THE CPI PRINT I AM NAMING AS MY EXIT IS ALSO THE LARGEST RISK TO THE POSITION AND IT CUTS AGAINST ME MORE OFTEN THAN FOR ME - traders are already pricing roughly a 60% chance of a Fed HIKE at the September 16 meeting after a strong jobs report, and higher real rates are the single most reliable negative for a non-yielding asset. A hot CPI on Friday raises hike odds and hits gold even though the inflation itself is nominally gold-positive; that is the trap in this trade. Gold FELL 1.1% on 9/8 while every energy name in this book rose, so the hedge has not actually been working in this episode. Newmont at 3.85x book and 16.2x earnings is not cheap, its 0.80% dividend gives no income support, and its asset base spans Papua New Guinea, Ghana, Suriname, Argentina and Peru - a jurisdictional risk set that has repeatedly produced single-name losses unrelated to the gold price. It sits 5.3% below its 135.29 52-week high from 8/25 and it has doubled off a 75.45 low set exactly one year ago today, so I am buying a very extended chart. First of three Non-Energy Minerals names. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 2: gold reverses to $4,435.60 from a $4,399 open, largest producer, hedge to the book's energy correlation

positions.name: Kinross Gold Corporation
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/10 open
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE CHEAPEST LARGE GOLD PRODUCER AND THE BEST PRE-MARKET CONFIRMATION IN THE GROUP: Kinross is quoted at 30.54 against a 30.15 close, +1.3%, which is the strongest pre-market move of the three gold names and it is being made on a tight 30.33/30.61 market rather than a stale print, on the same reversal in gold from a $4,399 open to $4,435.60 by 6:16am ET. At 11.68x trailing earnings it is materially cheaper than Newmont at 16.2x and AngloGold at 14.5x, and at a $35.8B market cap with a 1.18B share float it is liquid enough to trade properly. Its production base in the United States, Canada, Brazil, Chile and Mauritania is more weighted to OECD jurisdictions than AngloGold's African footprint. It sits 21.9% below its 39.11 52-week high from 1/26/2026, so of the three gold names this is the one where I am paying least for the chart.
positions.risks: I AM TAKING THREE GOLD MINERS AT ONCE, WHICH IS ONE COMMODITY VIEW EXPRESSED THREE TIMES AT ROUGHLY 15% OF THE BOOK, and Newmont, Kinross and AngloGold will not diverge in any scenario that matters - if the gold hedge fails on a hot 9/11 CPI and higher Fed hike odds, all three fail together and the book takes the loss on the same day the energy leg is also exposed to that print. Kinross's 21.9% discount to its January high is not free: it reflects a real cost-inflation problem at Tasiast and Paracatu and a market that assigns it a persistent discount for reserve life. The 0.50% dividend is the lowest of the three and offers no support. Volume of 6.24M on 9/8 ran only 0.75x its 8.35M 30-day average, the weakest participation of the three golds, and the stock closed at 30.15 after opening at 30.80 and touching 30.99 - it finished at the BOTTOM of its range on a day gold fell 1.1%, so the 9/8 tape was distribution and today's bid is a bounce off that, not a continuation. Overnight only.

positions.name: AngloGold Ashanti plc
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat by the 9/11 CPI release (8:30am ET) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THIRD GOLD NAME, HIGHEST INCOME SUPPORT, AND THE TIGHTEST QUOTED MARKET OF THE THREE: AngloGold is quoted at 108.27 against a 107.83 close on a 108.24/108.47 market - a 0.2% spread, the tightest pre-market pricing of anything I am adding today - on the same reversal in gold to $4,435.60. It carries a 4.14% dividend yield, more than five times Newmont's 0.80% and eight times Kinross's 0.50%, which is a genuine income floor under a position taken on a macro view rather than a company event, and it trades at 14.46x earnings between Kinross at 11.7x and Newmont at 16.2x. It sits 16.2% below its 129.14 52-week high from 3/2/2026. The catalyst-defined exit is the same 9/11 CPI print at 8:30am ET that governs the Newmont position, with headline consensus at 3.4% and core at 2.4%.
positions.risks: AT 6.15x BOOK THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE OF THE THREE GOLD MINERS ON ASSETS DESPITE THE MIDDLE P/E, and the asset base is the real issue: Ghana, Guinea, Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Argentina and Brazil, which is the highest-risk jurisdictional mix of the three by some distance, with a live history of resource-nationalism, permitting and power-supply disruptions that reprice the equity independent of the gold price. A 4.14% yield on a miner is a function of a spot gold price near record highs and is not durable if gold mean-reverts. The move I am buying is +0.4%, less than a third of Kinross's, so on the day's evidence this is the weakest confirmation of the three. It also traded 1.82M shares on 9/8 against a 2.76M 30-day average - 0.66x, thin - and closed at 107.83 after opening at 108.78, another bottom-of-range close. Third of three gold names taking that sector to a 15% book weight on a single commodity view, and the 9/11 CPI I have named as the exit is as likely to trigger a stop as a profit. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Robinhood Markets, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/10 open
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 A LARGE BROKER PRICE-TARGET HIKE INSIDE 24 HOURS AND THE ONLY NON-COMMODITY, NON-DEFENCE NAME IN THE BOOK: Cantor Fitzgerald raised its Robinhood price target from $115 to $150 with an Overweight rating, a 30% increase published Tuesday, implying 27% upside from this morning's quote. Robinhood is quoted at 118.40 against a 117.34 close, +0.9%, on a very tight 118.24/118.39 market at 11:18 UTC, and it is doing that while QQQ is quoted down 0.42% - so it is outperforming a weak tape rather than riding one. The strategic reason to own it here is that it is the single diversifier available: every other position in this book is levered to crude, gold or defence procurement, and Robinhood's earnings driver is retail trading volume and net interest on customer cash, which actually BENEFITS from the higher-for-longer rate path that the 9/11 CPI risk implies - the one position that gains from the scenario that damages the gold leg.
positions.risks: THE PRICE ACTION FLATLY CONTRADICTED THE PRICE TARGET AND I NEED TO BE HONEST ABOUT IT: Cantor published the $150 target on Tuesday and Robinhood opened at 125.07, traded down all day to a 117.08 low and closed at 117.34 - a 6.2% DECLINE on the day of the upgrade, finishing 1.5% off its low on 26.06M shares against a 21.03M average. That is the market rejecting the call on heavy volume, and today's +0.9% is a dead-cat bounce off that decline, not confirmation. The rule I am working to asks for PT hikes 'with confirming price action' and this one does not have it, which makes this the weakest-evidence position in today's book and is why it is overnight only rather than a swing. Robinhood at 54.1x earnings and 11.58x book is priced for perfection, its revenue is heavily crypto- and options-volume dependent and therefore collapses in exactly the risk-off tape the CNN Fear & Greed reading of 40.5 is describing, and a single sell-side target is the lowest-quality catalyst category available. It sits 23.0% below its 153.86 52-week high from 10/6/2025. Overnight only.
